formulas.value: Panel Performance Ratio (PPR): PPR = \frac{MeasuredPowerW}{PowerRatedW} \times 100\%, \text{where MeasuredPowerW is the measured power output and PowerRatedW is the rated power of the panel.}

Panel Efficiency Loss Rate (PELR): PELR = \frac{CurrentEfficiencyPercent - InitialEfficiencyPercent}{Years\_Since\_Installation} \times 100\%, \text{where CurrentEfficiencyPercent is obtained from efficiency_profile.current_efficiency.curreffpct.}

Temperature Performance Coefficient Impact (TPCI): TPCI = PowerRatedW \times TempCoef \times (CellTempC - 25), \text{where TempCoef is the temperature coefficient and 25°C is the standard test condition temperature.}
Energy Production Efficiency (EPE): EPE = PPR \times (1 - SoilingLossPercent/100) \times (1 - CumulativeDegradationPercent/100), \text{where PPR is the Panel Performance Ratio.}
Inverter Efficiency Loss (IEL): IEL = MeasuredPowerW \times (1 - InverterEfficiencyPercent/100), \text{where InverterEfficiencyPercent is from power_metrics.inverteffpct.}

Fill Factor Degradation Rate (FFDR): FFDR = \frac{FillFactorInitial - FillFactorCurrent}{Years\_Since\_Installation} \times 100\%, \text{where FillFactorInitial and FillFactorCurrent are from the electrical table.}
Soiling Impact Factor (SIF): SIF = SoilingLossPercent / DustDensityGM2, \text{where higher values indicate greater sensitivity to dust accumulation.}
Maintenance Cost Efficiency (MCE): MCE = \frac{MaintenanceCostUSD + CleaningCostUSD + ReplacementCostUSD}{GenCapMW}, \text{where lower values indicate more cost-effective maintenance.}
Revenue Loss Rate (RLR): RLR = \frac{RevenueLossUSD}{GenCapMW}, \text{where higher values indicate greater financial impact from downtime.}

Irradiance Utilization Ratio (IUR): IUR = \frac{MeasuredPowerW / PanelAreaM2}{POAIrradianceWM2}, \text{where POAIrradianceWM2 is from irradiance_conditions.irradiance_types[3] and PanelAreaM2 is the area of the panel.}

Critical Performance Threshold: A solar panel is considered below critical performance threshold when its Panel Performance Ratio (PPR) falls below 80% of the expected value for its age, accounting for normal degradation.

Weather Severity Index: A composite index calculated from extreme values of temperature, humidity, wind speed, and precipitation, where higher values indicate more severe operating conditions and increased risk of performance issues.

Grid Stability Factor: A metric determined by the combination of Power Quality Index, Harmonic Distortion Percentage, and Power Factor, where values closer to 1.0 indicate better contribution to grid stability.

PowerRatedW (Panel Rated Power): Measured in watts (W), representing the maximum power output a panel can produce under Standard Test Conditions (STC). Values typically range from 250W for older models to 650W for newer high-efficiency panels.

PaneEffPct (Panel Efficiency Percentage): Expressed as a percentage, representing how much of the sun's energy hitting the panel is converted to electricity. Modern panels typically range from 15% to 23%, with premium models reaching up to 25%.

TempCoef (Temperature Coefficient): Expressed as a percentage per degree Celsius (usually negative), indicating how much a panel's power output decreases for each degree above 25°C. Typical values range from -0.25% to -0.50% per °C, with lower absolute values indicating better high-temperature performance.

CellTempC (Cell Temperature): Measured in degrees Celsius, representing the actual temperature of the solar cells during operation. Typically ranges from 40°C to 70°C depending on ambient conditions and panel design, with temperatures above 80°C potentially causing accelerated degradation.

FillFactor (Fill Factor): A dimensionless value between 0 and 1 representing the ratio of maximum power point (Vmp × Imp) to open-circuit voltage times short-circuit current (Voc × Isc). High-quality commercial panels typically have fill factors between 0.75 and 0.85.

SoilingLossPct (Soiling Loss Percentage): Expressed as a percentage of power output lost due to soiling. Clean panels have values near 0%, while heavily soiled panels in dusty environments may experience losses exceeding 15%. Typical values in maintained systems range from 2% to 5%.

AnnDegRate (Annual Degradation Rate): Expressed as a percentage, representing how much a panel's output decreases per year. Quality silicon panels typically degrade at 0.5% to 0.7% annually, while lower quality or certain thin-film technologies may degrade at rates above 1% annually.

CumDegPct (Cumulative Degradation Percentage): Expressed as a percentage, representing total performance degradation since installation. New panels start at 0%, while panels approaching end-of-life may have values of 15-20% or higher, with manufacturer warranties typically covering degradation up to 20% over 25 years.

POAIrradianceWM2 (Plane-of-Array Irradiance): Measured in watts per square meter (W/m²), representing the solar energy reaching the panel surface. Typical daytime values range from 200 W/m² on heavily overcast days to 1000+ W/m² under clear sky conditions at solar noon.

InvertEffPct (Inverter Efficiency Percentage): Expressed as a percentage, representing how much DC power from panels is successfully converted to AC power. Modern string inverters typically operate at 96-98% efficiency, while microinverters may range from 94-97% efficiency.
Temperature Adjusted Performance Ratio (TAPR): TAPR = PPR + (TPCI / PowerRatedW), where PPR is the Panel Performance Ratio and TPCI is the Temperature Performance Coefficient Impact.

Total System Loss (TSL): TSL = (PowerRatedW × CumDegPct/100) + (MeasuredPowerW × SoilingLossPct/100) + IEL, where IEL is the Inverter Efficiency Loss and CumDegPct is from efficiency_profile.degradation.cumdegpct.

Maintenance Return on Investment (MROI): MROI = RLR / MCE, where RLR is the Revenue Loss Rate and MCE is the Maintenance Cost Efficiency. Higher values indicate better return on maintenance investments.

Effective Performance Index (EPI): EPI = PPR × (1 - TSL/PowerRatedW) × (IUR/PaneEffPct), where PPR is the Panel Performance Ratio, TSL is the Total System Loss, and IUR is the Irradiance Utilization Ratio.

Normalized Degradation Index (NDI): NDI = PELR / AnnDegRate, where PELR is the Panel Efficiency Loss Rate and AnnDegRate is from efficiency_profile.degradation.anndegrate. Values above 1.0 indicate faster than expected degradation.

Weather Corrected Efficiency (WCE): WCE = CurrentEfficiencyPercent × (1 + TempCoef × (25 - CellTempC) / 100) × (1000 / POAIrradianceWM2), where CurrentEfficiencyPercent is from efficiency_profile.current_efficiency.curreffpct.
Expected Energy Yield (EEY): EEY = PowerRatedW × EPE × SIF × POAIrradianceWM2 / 1000, where EPE is the Energy Production Efficiency and SIF is the Soiling Impact Factor.
Grid Integration Quality (GIQ): GIQ = PWRQualIDX × (1 - power_metrics.harmdistpct/100) × power_metrics.invertpowfac, using PWRQualIDX from the inverter table.

Electrical Degradation Index (EDI): EDI = (FillFactorInitial - FillFactorCurrent)/FillFactorInitial + (VocInitialV - VocCurrV)/VocInitialV + (IscInitialA - IscCurrA)/IscInitialA, where higher values indicate more severe degradation.

Financial Impact of Degradation (FID): FID = GenCapMW × 1000 × NDI × PELR × ElectricityPricePerKWh × 24 × 365, where NDI is the Normalized Degradation Index and PELR is the Panel Efficiency Loss Rate.
Advanced Performance Degradation Alert: A panel requires urgent attention when its Normalized Degradation Index exceeds 1.5 and its TAPR is below the Critical Performance Threshold.
Optimal Cleaning Schedule: Cleaning should be scheduled when SIF × DustDensityGM2 exceeds the Soiling Cleaning Threshold or when Expected Energy Yield is reduced by more than 3% due to soiling.
High-Risk Weather Condition: Weather conditions are considered high-risk when the Weather Severity Index exceeds 7.0 and Cell Temperature exceeds the upper limit of the Optimal Performance Window.

End-of-Warranty Optimization: Panels should be evaluated for warranty claims when approaching warranty expiration if their Normalized Degradation Index exceeds 0.9 or if they fail to meet the Warranty Claim Threshold criteria.

Grid Export Quality Classification: Power export quality is classified as 'Premium' when Grid Integration Quality exceeds 0.95, 'Standard' when between 0.90 and 0.95, and 'Substandard' when below 0.90, with substandard exports potentially subject to utility penalties.

System Upgrade Candidate: A plant qualifies as an upgrade candidate when the Financial Impact of Degradation exceeds 10% of replacement cost and Effective Performance Index is below 0.85 for three consecutive months.

Inverter-Panel Compatibility Index: An inverter-panel combination is considered optimally compatible when the panel's Weather Corrected Efficiency stays within 5% of the manufacturer's specifications and the inverter's Inverter Efficiency Percentage exceeds 97%.

Environmental Stress Classification: Environmental stress is classified based on combining Weather Severity Index and exposure time outside the Optimal Performance Window, with high stress potentially accelerating the Panel Efficiency Loss Rate.

Total Economic Performance: A comprehensive economic evaluation combining Maintenance Return on Investment, Financial Impact of Degradation, and revenue generation adjusted by the Effective Performance Index, providing a single metric for financial performance.

Degradation Severity Classification: Panels are classified as 'High Degradation' if NDI exceeds 1.5, 'Moderate Degradation' if NDI is between 1.0 and 1.5, and 'Normal Degradation' if below 1.0.

formulas.value: Panel Performance Ratio (PPR): PPR = \frac{MeasuredPowerW}{PowerRatedW} \times 100\%, \text{where MeasuredPowerW is the measured power output and PowerRatedW is the rated power of the panel.}

Temperature Performance Coefficient Impact (TPCI): TPCI = PowerRatedW \times TempCoef \times (CellTempC - 25), \text{where TempCoef is the temperature coefficient and 25°C is the standard test condition temperature.}
Energy Production Efficiency (EPE): EPE = PPR \times (1 - SoilingLossPercent/100) \times (1 - CumulativeDegradationPercent/100), \text{where PPR is the Panel Performance Ratio.}

Critical Performance Threshold: A solar panel is considered below critical performance threshold when its Panel Performance Ratio (PPR) falls below 80% of the expected value for its age, accounting for normal degradation.

Weather Severity Index: A composite index calculated from extreme values of temperature, humidity, wind speed, and precipitation, where higher values indicate more severe operating conditions and increased risk of performance issues.

TempCoef (Temperature Coefficient): Expressed as a percentage per degree Celsius (usually negative), indicating how much a panel's power output decreases for each degree above 25°C. Typical values range from -0.25% to -0.50% per °C, with lower absolute values indicating better high-temperature performance.

AnnDegRate (Annual Degradation Rate): Expressed as a percentage, representing how much a panel's output decreases per year. Quality silicon panels typically degrade at 0.5% to 0.7% annually, while lower quality or certain thin-film technologies may degrade at rates above 1% annually.

CumDegPct (Cumulative Degradation Percentage): Expressed as a percentage, representing total performance degradation since installation. New panels start at 0%, while panels approaching end-of-life may have values of 15-20% or higher, with manufacturer warranties typically covering degradation up to 20% over 25 years.
Temperature Adjusted Performance Ratio (TAPR): TAPR = PPR + (TPCI / PowerRatedW), where PPR is the Panel Performance Ratio and TPCI is the Temperature Performance Coefficient Impact.

Effective Performance Index (EPI): EPI = PPR × (1 - TSL/PowerRatedW) × (IUR/PaneEffPct), where PPR is the Panel Performance Ratio, TSL is the Total System Loss, and IUR is the Irradiance Utilization Ratio.
Advanced Performance Degradation Alert: A panel requires urgent attention when its Normalized Degradation Index exceeds 1.5 and its TAPR is below the Critical Performance Threshold.
High-Risk Weather Condition: Weather conditions are considered high-risk when the Weather Severity Index exceeds 7.0 and Cell Temperature exceeds the upper limit of the Optimal Performance Window.

System Upgrade Candidate: A plant qualifies as an upgrade candidate when the Financial Impact of Degradation exceeds 10% of replacement cost and Effective Performance Index is below 0.85 for three consecutive months.

Environmental Stress Classification: Environmental stress is classified based on combining Weather Severity Index and exposure time outside the Optimal Performance Window, with high stress potentially accelerating the Panel Efficiency Loss Rate.

Total Economic Performance: A comprehensive economic evaluation combining Maintenance Return on Investment, Financial Impact of Degradation, and revenue generation adjusted by the Effective Performance Index, providing a single metric for financial performance.

Maintenance Return on Investment (MROI): MROI = RLR / MCE, where RLR is the Revenue Loss Rate and MCE is the Maintenance Cost Efficiency. Higher values indicate better return on maintenance investments.

Premium Maintenance Candidate: A panel is considered a premium maintenance candidate when its Maintenance Return on Investment exceeds 2.0 and its Energy Production Efficiency is below 90% but above 75%.
